messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager — potential KV namespace shadow-read detected for customer-779 (dedicated-vpc pool 42). Severity: P1. Hits: 27 anomalous read events within last 5m. Trace-id: 0x7a3d9f. @Maya (oncall) paged.

Maya (oncall): on it. attaching initial impact matrix — do we have proof of cross-tenant payload yet or just path anomalies?

Jordan SRE: early signal looks like reads correlated with worker node node-gpu-042 in pool-42. No obvious auth bypass in app logs. Getting KV access logs now.

LogBot: KV access sample (sanitized):
```
ts=2024-05-03T14:12:01Z trace=0x7a3d9f svc=kv-read tenant=customer-779 key_prefix=/responses/1234 size=4
ts=2024-05-03T14:12:02Z trace=0x7a3d9f svc=kv-read tenant=customer-824 key_prefix=/responses/1234 size=4
# note: two tenants hitting same prefix within 1s window from same host ip
```

Devon Eng: that pattern looks like late-bind prefix aliasing — routing layer returned a backend that still used an old prefix table. Could be a stale prefix map on the inference proxy (htproxy).

Maya (oncall): does NSS or route caching have per-tenant TTLs? Could a recent rollout of prefix-map-v2 cause a split-brain?

Ravi (eng-runtime): prefix-map TTL is 60s by default. We rolled prefix-map-v2 to pool-42 earlier in the deploy window (13:50 UTC). I'm seeing a partial propagation: 8/12 nodes have updated map, 4 still on v1. There's a known fallback where requests hitting v1 can be routed to a different tenant's backend if keyspace overlap exists.

Jordan SRE: capturing kube exec output from node-gpu-042:
```
$ kubectl -n infra exec node-gpu-042 -- cat /var/run/prefix-map/version
v1
$ curl -s http://localhost:8080/prefix-map | jq .revision
1567
```

Devon Eng: mitigation proposal (short): 1) Quarantine node-gpu-042 from pool-42 routing; 2) Force-update prefix-map on remaining v1 nodes; 3) Throttle/redirect traffic from impacted tenant to fallback variant.

Maya (oncall): agree. immediate steps? I'm handing to Jordan for live mitigation. Amy, please prepare holding comms for customer-779 and let them know we're investigating and throttling affected requests.

Amy (acct): on it. Drafting message: "We are investigating an internal routing inconsistency affecting some requests. No evidence of persisted data exposure seen at this time; we're rate-limiting the impacted endpoints while we mitigate." Want ops wording or stronger?

Jordan SRE: executing quarantine now — running drain + route-blacklist on node-gpu-042.
```
# drain node from runtime pool
redwoodctl node drain --node node-gpu-042 --pool pool-42 --reason "prefix-map mismatch - quarantine"
# apply temporary route blacklist for node
redwoodctl route blacklist --node node-gpu-042 --prefix "/responses/" --ttl 600
```

LogBot: drain job queued (job-id: drain-20240503-14-17). Route blacklist applied.

Ravi (eng-runtime): pushing global prefix-map rev-sync to remaining nodes (force). Patch: prefix-map-v2 -> ensure strict tenant namespacing enforcement.

Devon Eng: before we roll, quick note — do NOT mass-restart the pool; restarts will trigger cold-cache KV reads and could increase blast radius. Use socket-level drain and route blacklisting only.

Maya (oncall): agreed. keep restarts as last resort. Jordan, capture all evidence and ship to vault S3-bucket (secure-evidence/customer-779/1712345678). We'll need it for postmortem and potential customer SOC review.

Jordan SRE: evidence archived. grep output attached (sanitized). I also captured the htproxy route table dumps from v1 nodes. Extract:
```
# snippet: route table v1 (node-gpu-042)
{ "prefix": "/responses/", "tenant_bind": "late-lookup", "backend": "be-824" }
# snippet: route table v2 (node-gpu-045)
{ "prefix": "/responses/", "tenant_bind": "strict", "backend": "be-779" }
```

Maya (oncall): ok looks like definitive evidence of inconsistent binding. What's customer visible impact? percent errors/latency?

Jordan SRE: customer-779 saw ~0.2% anomalous reads (27 events) over 10k requests in 5 minutes. No writes observed. Payloads were non-sensitive artifact fragments (debug tokens), masked by default. Logging indicates no downstream PII keys.

Amy (acct): giving customer-779 a heads up: "We're rate-limiting affected endpoints; our initial analysis shows limited read anomalies with no write or PII exposure. We're quarantining affected nodes and will follow up with a full timeline within 24h."

Ravi (eng-runtime): rolling force-sync complete. All nodes report prefix-map rev 1582. Verified namespace enforcement flags set to strict-mode.

LogBot: route-blacklist for node-gpu-042 expired in 590s — manual removal required after validation.

Devon Eng: recommend a quick canary test: issue 1000 requests against customer-779 endpoint verifying tenant header enforcement and KV namespace separation. I can run that now in isolated staging.

Maya (oncall): go ahead and run canary. Jordan, don't unquarantine until canary passes and we have at least 10 minutes of clean metrics.

Devon Eng: canary run results: 0/1000 cross-tenant reads, latencies stable.

Jordan SRE: metrics look clean on pool-42 post-sync. Unquarantine scheduled in 10m. Keeping route-blacklist until after final verification.

Maya (oncall): planning notes for incident timeline: - 13:50 UTC deploy prefix-map-v2 (partial) - 14:12 UTC anomalous reads observed - 14:16 UTC pager fired - 14:18 UTC quarantine node-gpu-042 + blacklist - 14:28 UTC force sync to remaining nodes - 14:45 UTC canary run passed - 15:00 UTC unquarantine started - 15:10 UTC customer notified initial findings

Amy (acct): customer acked receipt and asked for formal post-incident report and whether this affects contractual isolation guarantees. I'll coordinate escalation to legal if needed.

Ravi (eng-runtime): follow-ups we need to file as action items: 1) add preflight gating for prefix-map rollout ensuring >95% rev-sync before traffic shift, 2) add an automated rollback if any route-table mismatch is detected, 3) add metric alert for same-host cross-tenant read spikes.

Devon Eng: I'll own the postmortem for the runtime changes. Jordan will attach evidence and timelines. Maya will coordinate customer comms and severity justification. Amy will lead customer liaison.

Maya (oncall): handing to Ravi for final confirm and to close this oncall thread — please open a follow-up incident ticket for the postmortem and link it here. Good job team. :thumbsup:

Ravi (eng-runtime): opened INC-2024-779-ksync with links to evidence and assigned Devon as lead. Marking thread resolved on ops side.

IncidentBot: Incident update: status -> mitigated. All pages silenced.

Maya (oncall): closing thread — will add final notes to the ticket after 24h cool-down.
